# MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

**DRAFT: Provider Draft for Discussion. Subject to Negotiation.**

This Master Services Agreement (this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of January 1, 2027 (the "**Effective Date**") by and between **Harrowgate Home Goods, Inc.**, a New York corporation with its principal place of business in New York, New York ("**Customer**"), and **Bellweather Freight Logistics LLC**, a limited liability company ("**Provider**"). Customer and Provider are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## Recitals

A. Customer is a retailer of furniture and housewares and requires warehousing, freight transportation and delivery services in support of its retail and e-commerce operations.

B. Provider is in the business of providing warehousing, freight transportation and last-mile delivery services.

C. The Parties wish to set out the terms on which Provider will perform services for Customer under one or more statements of work.

The Parties therefore agree as follows:

## 1. Definitions

1.1 "**Affiliate**" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a Party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.

1.2 "**Customer Goods**" means all merchandise, inventory, fixtures and other goods of Customer or its Affiliates that are tendered to, received by, or in the possession, custody or control of Provider in connection with the Services.

1.3 "**Customer Data**" means all data and information, including Personal Data, that Customer or its end customers provide to Provider, or that Provider collects, generates or processes, in connection with the Services.

1.4 "**Data Processing Addendum**" or "**DPA**" means the Data Processing Addendum entered into between the Parties in connection with this Agreement, as amended from time to time.

1.5 "**Fees**" means the fees and charges payable by Customer for the Services as set out in the applicable Statement of Work.

1.6 "**Personal Data**" has the meaning given in the Data Processing Addendum.

1.7 "**Services**" means the warehousing, freight transportation, last-mile delivery and related services described in a Statement of Work.

1.8 "**Statement of Work**" or "**SOW**" means a statement of work executed by both Parties that references this Agreement and describes Services to be performed by Provider, including Statement of Work No. 1.

1.9 "**Term**" has the meaning given in Section 14.2.

## 2. Structure of Agreement

2.1 **Statements of Work.** Provider shall perform the Services described in each Statement of Work signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. Each Statement of Work is governed by and incorporates the terms of this Agreement.

2.2 **Contents of Statements of Work.** Each Statement of Work shall describe, as applicable, the Services, the facilities and service area, the start date, service levels, the Fees and any assumptions or Customer dependencies.

2.3 **Order of Precedence.** In the event of any conflict or inconsistency among the documents making up the Parties' agreement, the following order of precedence shall apply: the Data Processing Addendum, then this Agreement, then the Statement of Work.

2.4 **Change Orders.** Either Party may request a change to the scope of Services under a Statement of Work. No change shall be binding unless set out in a written change order signed by both Parties that states any resulting adjustment to the Fees or schedule.

## 3. Services

3.1 **Performance Standard.** Provider shall perform the Services in a diligent, professional and workmanlike manner, in accordance with the applicable Statement of Work, good industry practice for third-party logistics providers, and all applicable laws, regulations and permits.

3.2 **Exclusivity.** During the Term, Customer appoints Provider as Customer's exclusive provider of all warehousing, freight transportation and delivery services required by Customer and its Affiliates throughout the United States. During the Term, Customer shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, engage, contract with or use any third party to perform, or perform itself, any warehousing, freight transportation or delivery services throughout the United States.

3.3 **Service Levels.** Provider shall meet or exceed the service levels set out in each Statement of Work. If Provider fails to meet a service level, Provider shall (a) promptly notify Customer, (b) investigate and report the root cause, and (c) implement a corrective action plan reasonably acceptable to Customer. Any service credits set out in a Statement of Work shall be credited against the next invoice.

3.4 **Facilities and Equipment.** Unless otherwise stated in a Statement of Work, Provider shall furnish at its own cost all facilities, vehicles, equipment, materials, systems and personnel necessary to perform the Services, and shall maintain all such facilities, vehicles and equipment in safe, clean and good working order.

3.5 **Reporting.** Provider shall provide Customer with the inventory, shipment, delivery and exception reports described in each Statement of Work, and such other reports as Customer may reasonably request.

## 4. Customer Responsibilities

4.1 Customer shall provide Provider with accurate forecasts, shipping instructions, delivery addresses and product information reasonably required for Provider to perform the Services.

4.2 Customer shall ensure that Customer Goods tendered to Provider are properly packaged and labeled in accordance with the specifications in the applicable Statement of Work and do not include hazardous materials except as disclosed to and accepted by Provider in writing.

4.3 Customer shall designate a relationship manager who will serve as Provider's primary point of contact for the Services.

## 5. Fees and Payment

5.1 **Fees.** Customer shall pay the Fees set out in each Statement of Work. Fees exclude ap

plicable sales, use and similar taxes, which shall be invoiced separately and paid by Customer, other than taxes based on Provider's net income, property or employees.

5.2 **Invoicing.** Provider shall invoice Customer monthly in arrears unless a Statement of Work provides otherwise. Each invoice shall include reasonable supporting detail for all Fees and pass-through charges.

5.3 **Payment.** Customer shall pay each undisputed invoice within forty-five (45) days after receipt.

5.4 **Disputed Amounts.** Customer may withhold any invoiced amount that it disputes in good faith by notifying Provider in writing of the dispute and the basis for it before the payment due date. The Parties shall work in good faith to resolve the dispute within thirty (30) days. Provider shall continue performing the Services during any such dispute.

5.5 **Audit.** Provider shall maintain complete and accurate records relating to the Fees and the Services for at least three (3) years after the relevant invoice. Customer or its independent auditor may audit such records once per calendar year on reasonable advance notice during normal business hours.

## 6. Customer Goods

6.1 **Title.** Title to Customer Goods shall at all times remain with Customer. Provider has no right, title or interest in Customer Goods, and Provider shall keep Customer Goods free of all liens, claims and encumbrances arising by, through or under Provider, other than any lien that cannot be waived under applicable law.

6.2 **Care and Custody.** Provider shall exercise such care with respect to Customer Goods in its possession, custody or control as a reasonably careful warehouse operator and carrier would exercise under like circumstances, and shall store Customer Goods segregated from or readily identifiable apart from goods of other customers.

6.3 **Loss and Damage.** Provider shall be responsible for loss of or damage to Customer Goods occurring while in Provider's possession, custody or control, except to the extent caused by Customer's acts or omissions or by inherent defect in the Customer Goods. Provider shall reimburse Customer for such loss or damage at Customer's landed cost, as further described in the applicable Statement of Work.

6.4 **Inventory Counts.** Provider shall conduct cycle counts and an annual physical inventory as set out in the applicable Statement of Work, and Customer may attend any physical inventory.

## 7. Personnel and Subcontractors

7.1 **Personnel.** Provider shall assign qualified, trained and properly licensed personnel to perform the Services. Provider shall conduct background checks, consistent with applicable law, on all personnel who will enter end customers' residences.

7.2 **Subcontractors.** Provider shall not subcontract any material portion of the Services without Customer's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. Provider shall remain responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors as if they were Provider's own.

7.3 **Independent Contractor.** Provider is an independent contractor. Provider is solely responsible for the wages, benefits, taxes and supervision of its personnel, and nothing in this Agreement creates an employment, partnership, agency or joint venture relationship between the Parties.

## 8. Confidentiality

8.1 **Definition.** "**Confidential Information**" means any non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of a Party (the "**Discloser**") to the other Party (the "**Recipient**") that is marked or identified as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential. Customer Data and the terms of this Agreement are Customer's Confidential Information.

8.2 **Obligations.** The Recipient shall (a) use the Discloser's Confidential Information only to perform its obligations or exercise its rights under this Agreement, (b) protect it with at least the degree of care it uses for its own information of similar nature, and in no event less than reasonable care, and (c) disclose it only to its and its Affiliates' employees, contractors and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than this Section 8.

8.3 **Exclusions.** Confidential Information does not include information that the Recipient can show (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the Recipient, (b) was lawfully known to the Recipient before disclosure, (c) is lawfully received from a third party without restriction, or (d) is independently developed without use of the Discloser's Confidential Information.

8.4 **Compelled Disclosure.** The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by law or court order, provided it gives the Discloser prompt notice (where legally permitted) and reasonable cooperation so that the Discloser may seek a protective order.

8.5 **Return or Destruction.** On termination or expiration of this Agreement, or on the Discloser's request, the Recipient shall return or destroy the Discloser's Confidential Information, subject to the Data Processing Addendum in the case of Customer Data.

## 9. Data Protection

9.1 Provider shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions and in accordance with the Data Processing Addendum, which is incorporated into this Agreement by reference.

9.2 Provider shall implement and maintain appropriate administrative, technical and physical safeguards to protect Customer Data against unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration or destruction, as further described in the Data Processing Addendum.

9.3 Provider shall notify Customer of any security incident affecting Customer Data within the time and in the manner set out in the Data Processing Addendum.

## 10. Indemnification

10.1 **By Provider.** Provider shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors and employees from and against all losses, damages, l

iabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of any third-party claim to the extent arising from (a) bodily injury, death or damage to real or tangible personal property caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of Provider or its personnel or subcontractors in performing the Services, (b) Provider's violation of applicable law, or (c) any claim by Provider's personnel or subcontractors for wages, benefits or employment-related amounts.

10.2 **By Customer.** Customer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Provider, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, members and employees from and against all losses, damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of or relating to any third-party claim arising out of or relating to (a) Customer Goods, including any claim that Customer Goods are defective, unsafe or infringe any third-party right, (b) any Customer premises or end-customer premises at which Provider performs Services, or (c) Customer's use of the Services.

10.3 **Procedure.** The indemnified Party shall (a) give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim, provided that any delay shall relieve the indemnifying Party of its obligations only to the extent it is materially prejudiced, (b) give the indemnifying Party sole control of the defense and settlement of the claim, and (c) provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense. The indemnifying Party shall not settle any claim in a manner that imposes any obligation or admission on the indemnified Party without its prior written consent. The indemnified Party may participate with counsel of its choice at its own expense.

## 11. Limitation of Liability

11.1 **Liability Cap.** Except as set out in Section 11.3, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement and all Statements of Work, whether in contract, tort (including negligence) or otherwise, shall not exceed the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim.

11.2 **Exclusion of Indirect Damages.** Except as set out in Section 11.3, neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential, exemplary or punitive damages, or for lost profits or lost revenue, arising out of or relating to this Agreement, even if advised of the possibility of such damages.

11.3 **Exceptions.** The limitations in Sections 11.1 and 11.2 shall not apply to Customer's obligations under Section 10.2, which shall apply without limitation. The limitations in Sections 11.1 and 11.2 shall also not apply to either Party's liability for fraud, gross negligence or willful misconduct, or to Customer's obligation to pay Fees properly due.

## 12. Insurance

12.1 During the Term and for one (1) year thereafter, Provider shall maintain, at its own expense, with insurers rated A- VII or better by A.M. Best, at least the following insurance:

(a) commercial general liability insurance with limits of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and $4,000,000 in the aggregate;

(b) commercial automobile liability insurance covering all owned, hired and non-owned vehicles with a combined single limit of not less than $5,000,000 per accident;

(c) warehouse legal liability insurance with limits of not less than $5,000,000 per occurrence;

(d) motor truck cargo insurance with limits of not less than $250,000 per vehicle;

(e) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law and employer's liability insurance with limits of not less than $1,000,000 per accident; and

(f) cyber liability insurance with limits of not less than $3,000,000 per claim.

12.2 Provider shall name Customer as an additional insured on the policies described in Sections 12.1(a) and 12.1(b), and shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing the required coverage before the start date of the first Statement of Work and on each renewal of such coverage. Provider shall give Customer at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice of cancellation or material reduction of any required coverage.

## 13. Intellectual Property

13.1 Each Party retains all right, title and interest in its pre-existing materials, systems, software and intellectual property.

13.2 Customer owns all Customer Data and all reports prepared by Provider specifically for Customer under this Agreement. Provider grants Customer a non-exclusive, royalty-free license during the Term to use any Provider portal or system made available to Customer in connection with the Services.

13.3 Customer grants Provider a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license during the Term to use Customer's names and marks solely as necessary to perform the Services, including on delivery documentation.

## 14. Term and Termination

14.1 **Initial Term.** This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of 2 years from the MSA Effective Date (the "**Initial Term**"), unless terminated earlier in accordance with this Section 14.

14.2 **Renewal.** On expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive renewal terms of three (3) years each (each, a "**Renewal Term**" and, together with the Initial Term, the "**Term**"), unless either Party delivers written notice of non-renewal to the other Party during the fifteen (15) day period ending one hundred twenty (120) days before the expiry of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term. Notice of non-renewal delivered at any other time shall be of no effect.

14.3 **Termination for Cause.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work by written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement or that Statement of Work and fails to cure the breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice describing it.

14.4 **Insolvency.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if the o

ther Party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, has a receiver appointed for all or substantially all of its assets, or becomes the subject of any bankruptcy proceeding that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days.

14.5 **Effect on Statements of Work.** Termination or expiration of this Agreement shall terminate all Statements of Work then in effect, unless the Parties agree otherwise in writing.

## 15. Effect of Termination; Transition

15.1 On termination or expiration of this Agreement or any Statement of Work, Provider shall (a) promptly release and make available for collection all Customer Goods in its possession, custody or control, (b) return Customer Data in accordance with the Data Processing Addendum, and (c) provide final inventory reconciliation reports.

15.2 At Customer's request, Provider shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to ninety (90) days after termination or expiration to enable an orderly transfer of the Services to Customer or its designee, at the rates set out in the applicable Statement of Work.

15.3 Customer shall pay all undisputed Fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination or expiration.

15.4 Sections 5.5, 6.1, 8, 10, 11, 13.1, 15, 17 and 18, and any other provision that by its nature is intended to survive, shall survive termination or expiration of this Agreement.

## 16. Representations and Warranties

16.1 **Mutual.** Each Party represents and warrants that (a) it is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization, (b) it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, and (c) its execution and performance of this Agreement do not conflict with any other agreement by which it is bound.

16.2 **By Provider.** Provider represents and warrants that (a) it holds, and will maintain throughout the Term, all licenses, registrations, operating authorities and permits required to perform the Services, including any required federal motor carrier operating authority, and (b) it will perform the Services in compliance with all applicable laws.

16.3 **Disclaimer.** Except as expressly set out in this Agreement, neither Party makes any other warranty, express or implied.

## 17. General

17.1 **Notices.** All notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the addresses stated on the signature page, with a copy by email. Notices are effective on receipt. Either Party may change its notice address by notice to the other Party.

17.2 **Force Majeure.** Neither Party shall be liable for any delay or failure to perform (other than payment obligations) caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including acts of God, flood, fire, epidemic, war, terrorism, civil unrest or governmental action, provided that the affected Party promptly notifies the other Party and uses commercially reasonable efforts to resume performance. If a force majeure event prevents Provider from performing a material portion of the Services for more than fifteen (15) days, Customer may procure substitute services for the duration of the event.

17.3 **Compliance.** Each Party shall comply with all applicable laws in performing this Agreement, including anti-corruption, export control and employment laws.

17.4 **Assignment.** Customer shall not assign, delegate or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any Statement of Work, or any of its rights or obligations under them, whether voluntarily, by operation of law, by merger or change of control or otherwise, without Provider's prior written consent. Any purported assignment in violation of this Section 17.4 is void. This Agreement binds and benefits the Parties and their permitted successors and assigns.

17.5 **Amendment and Waiver.** This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. No waiver is effective unless in writing, and no failure or delay in exercising any right operates as a waiver of it.

17.6 **Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, that provision shall be enforced to the maximum extent permissible and the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect.

17.7 **No Third-Party Beneficiaries.** Except for the indemnified persons under Section 10, nothing in this Agreement confers any right or remedy on any person other than the Parties.

17.8 **Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument.

## 18. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution

18.1 **Governing Law and Forum.** This Agreement and any dispute arising out of or relating to it shall be governed by and construed in accordance with New York law, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, New York, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

18.2 **Escalation.** Before commencing any proceeding (other than for urgent injunctive relief), a Party shall give written notice of the dispute to the other Party, and senior executives of each Party shall meet within fifteen (15) business days in a good-faith attempt to resolve it.

18.3 **Injunctive Relief.** Each Party acknowledges that a breach of Section 8 or Section 9 may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be inadequate, and that the non-breaching Party may seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedy.

18.4 **Waiver of Jury Trial.** EACH PARTY KNOWINGLY AND VOLUNTARILY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY PROCEEDING ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT.

# STATEMENT OF WORK NO. 1

**Warehousing and Last-Mile Delivery Services**

**DRAFT: Provider Draft for Discussion. Subject to Negotiation.**

This Statement of Work No. 1 (this "**SOW**") is entered into under the Master Services Agreement dated as of January 1, 2027 (the "**Agreement**") by and between **Harrowgate Home Goods, Inc.** ("**Customer**") and **Bellweather Freight Logistics LLC** ("**Provider**"). This SOW is governed by and incorporates the terms of the Agreement. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this SOW have the meanings given in the Agreement.

## 1. Purpose and Scope

1.1 **Purpose.** This SOW describes the warehousing, fulfillment and last-mile home delivery Services that Provider will perform for Customer in support of Customer's retail store replenishment and e-commerce operations in the Service Area.

1.2 **In-Scope Services.** The Services under this SOW consist of:

(a) receiving, inspecting, storing and managing Customer Goods at the Facility (Section 3);

(b) order fulfillment, including picking, packing, staging and loading of Customer Goods for store replenishment and for delivery to end customers (Section 3);

(c) last-mile home delivery of Customer Goods to end customers within the Service Area, including threshold, room-of-choice and white-glove delivery options (Section 4);

(d) basic assembly, debris removal and haul-away of packaging, where ordered by Customer for a particular delivery (Section 4); and

(e) reporting, inventory control and returns processing as described in this SOW.

1.3 **Out-of-Scope Services.** Any service not described in this SOW, including line-haul transportation outside the Service Area, is outside the scope of this SOW and may be added only by a change order under Section 2.4 of the Agreement or by a separate Statement of Work.

## 2. Start Date and Term

2.1 **Start Date.** Provider shall commence the Services on January 15, 2027 (the "**Start Date**").

2.2 **Implementation.** Between the Effective Date of the Agreement and the Start Date, Provider shall complete the implementation activities set out in Schedule A, including warehouse management system configuration, integration with Customer's order management system, and receipt of the initial inventory transfer from Customer's current facility.

2.3 **Term of SOW.** This SOW continues from the Start Date until the expiration or termination of the Agreement, unless terminated earlier in accordance with Section 14 of the Agreement.

## 3. Warehousing and Fulfillment

3.1 **Facility.** Provider shall perform the warehousing and fulfillment Services at its distribution center located at 400 Meadowlands Parkway, Secaucus, New Jersey (the "**Facility**"). Provider shall not relocate the Services to another facility without Customer's prior written consent.

3.2 **Dedicated Space.** Provider shall make available to Customer not less than 180,000 square feet of racked and floor storage space at the Facility, of which not less than 40,000 square feet shall be suitable for oversized furniture items. Customer Goods shall be stored segregated from or readily identifiable apart from goods of other customers in accordance with Section 6.2 of the Agreement.

3.3 **Receiving.** Provider shall unload, count and visually inspect all inbound shipments of Customer Goods and post receipts to the warehouse management system within twenty-four (24) hours after arrival at the Facility. Provider shall note any visible damage or shortage on the carrier's delivery receipt and report it to Customer within one (1) business day.

3.4 **Packaging and Labeling.** Customer Goods tendered to Provider shall be packaged and labeled in accordance with Customer's Vendor Packaging and Labeling Guide, as provided to Provider before the Start Date and updated by Customer on reasonable notice, for purposes of Section 4.2 of the Agreement.

3.5 **Order Fulfillment.** Provider shall pick, pack and stage (a) e-commerce orders received by 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time on a business day for delivery on the scheduled delivery date, and (b) store replenishment orders in accordance with the weekly replenishment schedule agreed by the Parties' relationship managers.

3.6 **Inventory Counts.** For purposes of Section 6.4 of the Agreement, Provider shall conduct (a) daily cycle counts such that every storage location is counted at least once per calendar quarter, and (b) one annual physical inventory during January of each year on a date agreed with Customer at least thirty (30) days in advance.

3.7 **Returns.** Provider shall receive, inspect and grade returned Customer Goods within two (2) business days after receipt, and shall restock, quarantine or dispose of returned Customer Goods in accordance with Customer's written disposition instructions.

## 4. Last-Mile Delivery

4.1 **Service Area.** Provider shall perform last-mile home delivery to end customers located within the five boroughs of New York City and Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester and Rockland Counties, New York, and Bergen, Hudson, Essex and Union Counties, New Jersey (the "**Service Area**").

4.2 **Delivery Options.** Provider shall offer the following delivery service levels, as selected by Customer or its end customer at the time of order:

(a) **Threshold:** delivery to the first dry area inside the residence entrance;

(b) **Room of Choice:** delivery to a room selected by the end customer, including carrying up to three (3) flights of stairs; and

(c) **White Glove:** room-of-choice delivery plus unpacking, placement, basic assembly of items that do not require tools beyond those carried on the vehicle, and removal of all packaging debris.

4.3 **Scheduling.** Provider shall contact each end customer at least forty-eight (48) hours before the scheduled delivery date to confirm a four (4) hour delivery window, and shall send a text or email notification when the delivery vehicle is within approximately thirty (30) minutes of the end customer's address.

4.4 **Delivery Personnel.** Each delivery shall be performed by a crew of at least two (2) persons for any item weighing more than seventy-five (75) pounds. All personnel entering end customers' residences shall have passed background checks in accordance with Section 7.1 of the Agreement and shall wear Provider uniforms and identification.

4.5 **Proof of Delivery.** Provider shall obtain electronic proof of delivery, including the end customer's signature and time-stamped photographs of each delivered item in place, and shall make proof of delivery available to Customer through the Provider portal within two (2) hours after delivery.

4.6 **Damaged or Refused Items.** If an item is damaged on delivery or refused by the end customer, Provider shall return the item to the Facility, document the condition, and notify Customer within one (1) business day.

## 5. Fees

5.1 **Monthly Service Fee.** In consideration of the Services described in this SOW, Customer shall pay Provider a fixed monthly service fee of $184,500 per month (the "**Monthly Service Fee**"). The Monthly Service Fee covers (a) the dedicated storage space described in Section 3.2, (b) receiving, fulfillment and returns processing for up to the Baseline Volumes, and (c) last-mile delivery of up to the Baseline Volumes.

5.2 **Baseline Volumes.** The "**Baseline Volumes**" for each calendar month are: (a) 2,400 inbound pallets received; (b) 9,000 e-commerce orders fulfilled; and (c) 6,500 last-mile home deliveries completed, of which not more than 1,500 are White Glove deliveries.

5.3 **Excess Volume Charges.** Volumes in excess of the Baseline Volumes in any calendar month shall be charged at the following unit rates:

| Activity | Unit Rate |
|---|---|
| Inbound pallet received | $9.50 per pallet |
| E-commerce order fulfilled | $4.25 per order |
| Threshold delivery | $68.00 per delivery |
| Room of Choice delivery | $89.00 per delivery |
| White Glove delivery | $129.00 per delivery |
| Haul-away of end customer's existing furniture (where ordered) | $45.00 per item |

5.4 **Pro-Ration.** The Monthly Service Fee for January 2027 shall be pro-rated based on the number of days from the Start Date through January 31, 2027.

5.5 **Pass-Through Charges.** Bridge and tunnel tolls and congestion pricing charges incurred on deliveries within the Service Area shall be passed through to Customer at cost, without mark-up, and supported by itemized detail on the monthly invoice in accordance with Section 5.2 of the Agreement.

5.6 **Transition Assistance Rates.** Transition assistance requested by Customer under Section 15.2 of the Agreement shall be charged at the following rates: (a) operations manager, $115 per hour; (b) warehouse associate, $48 per hour; and (c) systems and data support, $140 per hour. Outbound handling of Customer Goods on release from the Facility shall be charged at the inbound pallet rate in Section 5.3.

5.7 **Invoicing and Payment.** Provider shall invoice the Monthly Service Fee, excess volume charges and pass-through charges monthly in arrears, and Customer shall pay each undisputed invoice in accordance with Section 5.3 of the Agreement.

## 6. Service Levels and Service Credits

6.1 **Service Levels.** Provider shall meet the following service levels, measured monthly:

| Service Level | Target |
|---|---|
| Receipt posting within 24 hours of arrival | 99.0% |
| Order fulfillment accuracy (correct item and quantity) | 99.5% |
| On-time delivery within confirmed four-hour window | 97.0% |
| Damage-free delivery | 99.0% |
| Inventory record accuracy (by location, at cycle count) | 99.5% |

6.2 **Service Credits.** For each service level that Provider fails to meet in a calendar month, Provider shall credit Customer an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Monthly Service Fee for that month, up to a maximum aggregate credit of ten percent (10%) of the Monthly Service Fee for that month. Service credits shall be applied against the next invoice in accordance with Section 3.3 of the Agreement and are without prejudice to Customer's other rights and remedies under the Agreement.

6.3 **Loss and Damage.** For purposes of Section 6.3 of the Agreement, "landed cost" means Customer's purchase price for the affected Customer Goods plus inbound freight, duties and customs charges actually incurred by Customer, as shown in Customer's records. Provider shall pay or credit any amount due for loss or damage within thirty (30) days after Customer's written claim with reasonable supporting documentation.

## 7. Reporting and Governance

7.1 **Reports.** Provider shall provide Customer with the following reports through the Provider portal, in addition to those required under Section 3.5 of the Agreement:

(a) daily inventory-on-hand and receiving reports;

(b) daily delivery completion and exception reports, including failed and rescheduled deliveries;

(c) weekly damage and claims reports; and

(d) a monthly service level scorecard showing performance against each service level in Section 6.1 and any resulting service credits.

7.2 **Governance.** Each Party's relationship manager shall meet weekly during the first ninety (90) days after the Start Date and monthly thereafter to review performance, forecasts and open issues. Senior representatives of each Party shall hold a quarterly business review.

7.3 **Customer Data.** Provider shall process end customer names, addresses, telephone numbers, email addresses and delivery instructions only as necessary to perform the Services under this SOW and in accordance with Section 9 of the Agreement and the Data Processing Addendum.

## 8. Subcontracting and Assignment

8.1 **Subcontracting.** Provider shall not subcontract any material portion of the Services under this SOW, including any last-mile delivery route, without Customer's prior written consent in accordance with Section 7.2 of the Agreement.

8.2 **Assignment by Provider.** Provider may assign, delegate or other

# DATA PROCESSING ADDENDUM

**DRAFT: Provider Draft for Discussion. Subject to Negotiation.**

This Data Processing Addendum (this "**DPA**") is entered into by and between **Harrowgate Home Goods, Inc.**, a New York corporation ("**Customer**"), and **Bellweather Freight Logistics LLC** ("**Provider**"), in connection with the Master Services Agreement dated as of January 1, 2027 between Customer and Provider (the "**Agreement**"). This DPA forms part of the Agreement. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this DPA have the meanings given in the Agreement.

## 1. Definitions

1.1 "**Data Protection Laws**" means all U.S. federal, state and local laws and regulations that apply to the Processing of Personal Data under the Agreement. These include, as applicable, the New York Stop Hacks and Improve Electronic Data Security Act (N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law § 899-aa and § 899-bb), the New Jersey Identity Theft Prevention Act and the New Jersey Data Privacy Act, the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act, and comparable state privacy and data breach notification laws.

1.2 "**Personal Data**" means any information included in Customer Data that identifies, relates to, describes, or is reasonably capable of being associated with an identified or identifiable natural person or household. This includes end customer names, delivery addresses, telephone numbers, email addresses, delivery instructions, signatures and proof-of-delivery photographs.

1.3 "**Process**" or "**Processing**" means any operation performed on Personal Data, whether or not by automated means. This includes collection, recording, organization, storage, retrieval, use, disclosure, transmission, combination, restriction, erasure and destruction.

1.4 "**Security Incident**" means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration, loss or destruction of, Personal Data or other Customer Data in Provider's or its Subprocessors' possession, custody or control.

1.5 "**Subprocessor**" means any third party, including any subcontractor or Provider Affiliate, that Provider engages to Process Personal Data on Provider's behalf.

## 2. Roles and Scope

2.1 **Roles.** Customer is the controller, or "business," of the Personal Data. Provider is a processor, or "service provider," that Processes Personal Data solely on Customer's behalf.

2.2 **Scope of Processing.** Provider shall Process Personal Data only to the extent necessary to perform the Services described in the applicable Statement of Work. Annex 1 describes the categories of data subjects, the categories of Personal Data, and the nature and purposes of the Processing.

2.3 **Duration.** Provider shall Process Personal Data for the Term of the Agreement and, after that, only as needed to complete the return or deletion obligations in Section 8.

## 3. Provider Obligations

3.1 **Instructions.** Provider shall Process Personal Data only on Customer's documented instructions. The Agreement, the applicable Statement of Work and this DPA constitute those instructions. Provider shall promptly inform Customer if, in Provider's opinion, an instruction violates Data Protection Laws.

3.2 **Restrictions.** Provider shall not:

(a) sell or share Personal Data, as those terms are defined in Data Protection Laws;

(b) retain, use or disclose Personal Data for any purpose other than performing the Services, including for any commercial purpose of Provider or for marketing to end customers;

(c) retain, use or disclose Personal Data outside the direct business relationship between Customer and Provider; or

(d) combine Personal Data with personal information that Provider receives from or on behalf of any other person, except as permitted by Data Protection Laws.

3.3 **Compliance.** Provider shall comply with all Data Protection Laws applicable to it as a service provider or processor. Provider shall provide the same level of privacy protection as those laws require. Provider shall notify Customer within five (5) business days if it determines that it can no longer meet its obligations under Data Protection Laws or this DPA.

3.4 **Personnel.** Provider shall ensure that all personnel authorized to Process Personal Data are bound by written confidentiality obligations. Such personnel may access Personal Data only to the extent needed to perform the Services.

3.5 **Location.** Provider shall Process and store Personal Data only within the United States. It may do so elsewhere only with Customer's prior written consent.

## 4. Security

4.1 **Safeguards.** For purposes of Section 9.2 of the Agreement, Provider shall implement and maintain a written information security program. That program shall include the administrative, technical and physical safeguards described in Annex 2. The safeguards shall be no less rigorous than the reasonable safeguards required by N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law § 899-bb.

4.2 **Devices and Delivery Records.** Personal Data on handheld devices, driver applications and delivery vehicles' electronic systems shall be encrypted. Those devices shall be capable of remote wipe. Printed manifests and delivery paperwork containing Personal Data shall be collected at the end of each route. They shall then be securely shredded or retained under lock.

4.3 **Review.** Provider shall review and test its safeguards at least annually. It shall promptly remediate any material deficiency identified.

## 5. Security Incidents

5.1 **Notice.** For purposes of Section 9.3 of the Agreement, Provider shall notify Customer in writing without undue delay, and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours, after becoming aware of a Security Incident.

5.2 **Contents of Notice.** The notice shall describe, to the extent known:

(a) the nature of the Security Incident;

(b) the categories and approximate number of individuals and records affected;

(c) the likely consequences; and

(d) the measures taken or propose

data_processing_addendum.md, page 2 of 3:
d to contain and remediate it.

Provider shall supplement the notice as more information becomes available.

5.3 **Cooperation.** Provider shall take all reasonable steps to contain, investigate and remediate each Security Incident. Provider shall cooperate with Customer's investigation and with any notifications Customer elects or is required to make.

5.4 **Notifications by Customer.** Customer shall determine whether to notify affected individuals, regulators or other third parties of a Security Incident, and the content of any such notice. Provider shall not make any such notification without Customer's prior written approval, except where Provider is independently required to do so by law.

5.5 **Costs.** Provider shall reimburse Customer's reasonable costs of investigating and responding to any Security Incident caused by a breach of this DPA by Provider or its Subprocessors. These costs include notification, call center and credit monitoring costs.

## 6. Subprocessors

6.1 **Consent.** Provider shall not engage any Subprocessor without Customer's prior written consent, consistent with Section 7.2 of the Agreement. Annex 3 lists the Subprocessors approved as of the date of this DPA.

6.2 **Subprocessor Terms.** Provider shall impose on each Subprocessor, by written contract, data protection obligations no less protective than those in this DPA.

6.3 **Responsibility.** Provider shall remain responsible for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions as if they were Provider's own.

## 7. Assistance, Records and Audits

7.1 **Consumer Requests.** Provider shall notify Customer within five (5) business days of receiving any request from an individual to exercise rights under Data Protection Laws. Provider shall not respond to the request except on Customer's instructions. Provider shall provide reasonable assistance so that Customer can respond to such requests.

7.2 **Regulatory Inquiries.** Provider shall promptly notify Customer of any inquiry from a governmental authority relating to Personal Data, to the extent legally permitted. Provider shall cooperate with Customer in responding.

7.3 **Audit.** On reasonable advance notice, Provider shall make available to Customer the information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with this DPA. This includes any current third-party security assessment or audit report. Customer or its independent auditor may conduct an on-site audit of Provider's Processing once per calendar year, and at any time following a Security Incident. Any such audit shall take place during normal business hours and shall be subject to reasonable confidentiality obligations.

7.4 **Remediation.** If Customer reasonably determines that Provider is Processing Personal Data in an unauthorized manner, Customer may take reasonable and appropriate steps to stop and remediate that Processing. Provider shall cooperate with those steps.

## 8. Return and Deletion

8.1 **On Termination.** For purposes of Sections 8.5 and 15.1 of the Agreement, Provider shall return Customer Data to Customer within thirty (30) days after termination or expiration of the Agreement or the applicable Statement of Work. The return shall be made in a commonly used, machine-readable format reasonably specified by Customer.

8.2 **Deletion.** After returning Customer Data, Provider shall securely delete all remaining copies of it, including copies held by Subprocessors. Provider shall certify the deletion in writing at Customer's request.

8.3 **Legal Retention.** Provider may retain Customer Data only to the extent required by applicable law. Any retained Customer Data shall remain subject to this DPA and the confidentiality obligations of the Agreement for as long as it is retained.

## 9. Governing Law and Jurisdiction

9.1 **Governing Law and Forum.** This DPA and any dispute arising out of or relating to it, including any dispute relating to the Processing of Personal Data or any Security Incident, shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

## 10. General

10.1 **Term.** This DPA takes effect on the Effective Date of the Agreement. It remains in effect for as long as Provider or any Subprocessor Processes Personal Data.

10.2 **Amendment.** The Parties shall negotiate in good faith any amendment to this DPA reasonably required to comply with changes in Data Protection Laws. This DPA may be amended only by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.

10.3 **Counterparts.** This DPA may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature.

# TERM SHEET

**Warehousing and Last-Mile Delivery Services**

**Harrowgate Home Goods, Inc. / Bellweather Freight Logistics LLC**

**Dated: September 22, 2026**

This term sheet (this "**Term Sheet**") summarizes the principal terms on which **Harrowgate Home Goods, Inc.**, a New York corporation ("**Customer**"), and **Bellweather Freight Logistics LLC** ("**Provider**") propose that Provider will provide warehousing, fulfillment and last-mile delivery services to Customer. Except as stated in Section 12, this Term Sheet is non-binding. It is intended only as a basis for preparing definitive agreements.

## 1. Parties

| Role | Party |
|---|---|
| Customer | Harrowgate Home Goods, Inc. |
| Provider | Bellweather Freight Logistics LLC |

## 2. Transaction Structure

2.1 The Parties will enter into a master services agreement (the "**MSA**") setting out the general terms of the relationship. Specific services will be described in one or more statements of work under the MSA, the first being Statement of Work No. 1 ("**SOW No. 1**"). The Parties will also enter into a data processing addendum governing Provider's processing of Customer's end-customer personal data (together with the MSA and SOW No. 1, the "**Definitive Agreements**").

2.2 Provider will prepare the initial drafts of the Definitive Agreements for Customer's review.

## 3. Services

3.1 **Warehousing and Fulfillment.** Receiving, storage, inventory control, order fulfillment, store replenishment and returns processing for Customer goods at Provider's distribution center at 400 Meadowlands Parkway, Secaucus, New Jersey.

3.2 **Last-Mile Home Delivery.** Threshold, room-of-choice and white-glove home delivery of Customer goods to Customer's end customers within the New York City metropolitan area, including basic assembly and debris removal where ordered.

3.3 **Service Levels.** SOW No. 1 will include monthly service levels for receipt posting, fulfillment accuracy, on-time delivery, damage-free delivery and inventory accuracy, supported by service credits.

## 4. Exclusivity

4.1 Customer will engage Provider on an exclusive basis for last-mile home delivery within the New York City metropolitan area only.

4.2 No other services are subject to exclusivity. Customer remains free to use other providers, or to perform services itself, for all warehousing, freight transportation, line-haul and delivery services outside the scope of Section 4.1.

## 5. Key Dates

| Item | Target |
|---|---|
| MSA effective date | January 1, 2027 |
| SOW No. 1 start date (go-live) | January 15, 2027 |
| Initial term of MSA | 2 years from the MSA effective date |

## 6. Fees

6.1 **Monthly Service Fee.** A fixed monthly service fee of $184,500 per month, covering dedicated storage space and baseline monthly volumes of inbound pallets, e-commerce orders and last-mile deliveries to be set out in SOW No. 1.

6.2 **Excess Volumes.** Volumes above the baseline will be charged at unit rates to be set out in SOW No. 1.

6.3 **Payment.** Monthly invoicing in arrears. Customer to pay undisputed amounts within forty-five (45) days after receipt and may withhold amounts disputed in good faith.

## 7. Customer Goods

Title to Customer goods remains with Customer at all times. Provider will be responsible for loss of or damage to Customer goods in its possession, custody or control, reimbursed at Customer's landed cost.

## 8. Liability and Insurance

8.1 **Liability Cap.** Each Party's aggregate liability will be capped at the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim, subject to customary exceptions to be agreed in the Definitive Agreements.

8.2 **Indemnities.** To be negotiated in the Definitive Agreements.

8.3 **Insurance.** Provider will maintain commercial general liability, automobile liability, warehouse legal liability, motor truck cargo, workers' compensation and cyber liability coverage at levels to be set out in the MSA, and will name Customer as an additional insured where customary.

## 9. Data Protection

Provider will process end-customer personal data only on Customer's instructions, solely to perform the services, within the United States, and in accordance with the data processing addendum. Provider will notify Customer promptly of any security incident affecting Customer data.

## 10. Term, Renewal and Assignment

10.1 Initial term as stated in Section 5.

10.2 Renewal, termination and assignment terms to be negotiated in the Definitive Agreements.

## 11. Governing Law

The Definitive Agreements will be governed by New York law, with disputes resolved in the state and federal courts in New York County, New York.

## 12. Non-Binding Effect; Binding Provisions

12.1 This Term Sheet does not create any legally binding obligation on either Party to enter into the Definitive Agreements or to perform or purchase any services. Binding obligations will arise only on execution of the Definitive Agreements.

12.2 Despite Section 12.1, the following provisions are binding on the Parties:

(a) **Confidentiality.** Each Party will keep the terms of this Term Sheet and all non-public information received from the other Party in connection with the proposed transaction confidential. Each Party will use such information only to evaluate and negotiate the proposed transaction.

(b) **Costs.** Each Party will bear its own costs and expenses in connection with this Term Sheet and the negotiation of the Definitive Agreements.

(c) **Governing Law.** This Section 12 is governed by New York law.

12.3 Either Party may end negotiations at any time by written notice to the other Party, without liability, except under the binding provisions in Section 12.2, which survive for two (2) years.
